items.title: Case (1): Modes of vibrations in an organ pipe open at both ends

source_refs.note: Case (1): Modes of vibrations in an organ pipe open at both ends: a main subheading of 7.6 Stationary waves in air columns, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 150-150.

blocks.text: Let us consider an organ pipe of length l which is open at both ends. As at the open end, an air molecule has complete freedom of motion so it acts as antinode as shown in Fig. 7.8. In this figure, longitudinal waves set up inside the pipe have been represented by transverse curved lines which represent the displacement and amplitude of vibration of air particles at various points along the axis of pipe.

In this case, as shown in Fig. 7.8 (a), there is only one node N at the middle of the pipe. As both ends of pipe are open, there are two antinodes at both the ends. If λ₁ is the wavelength of sound, then

(a) one node in the middle, l = lambda1/2, f1 = v/2l; (b) two nodes, l = 2(lambda2/2), f2 = 2(v/2l); (c) three nodes, l = 3(lambda3/2), f3 = 3(v/2l). Above (a) and (b), green double arrows mark the antinodes and dots the nodes.
